description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between Average Lagging (AL) on the x-axis and BLEU score on the y-axis for four different methods in simultaneous machine translation: Consistency-CE, Inconsistency-CE, Inconsistency-CE-MP, and Consistency-Bi. The x-axis, labeled “Average Lagging (AL),” ranges from 0 to 7 with tick marks at integer intervals (0, 2, 4, 6). The y-axis, labeled “BLEU,” spans from 12 to 28 with major gridlines every 2 units. The “Consistency-CE” method (purple line with circle markers, dashed) starts at approximately BLEU 12.8 at AL=0, rises to ~19.8 at AL=1, ~22.2 at AL=4, and ~26.2 at AL=7. The “Inconsistency-CE” method (purple line with square markers, solid) begins at ~20.0 at AL=1, increases to ~25.2 at AL=4, and reaches ~27.0 at AL=7. The “Inconsistency-CE-MP” method (blue line with square markers, dashed) starts at ~20.0 at AL=1, rises to ~25.2 at AL=4, and ends at ~27.0 at AL=7, closely tracking Inconsistency-CE. The “Consistency-Bi” method (red line with star markers, solid) begins at ~22.6 at AL=1, increases to ~25.8 at AL=4, and reaches ~28.0 at AL=7, consistently outperforming the others across the range. All methods show a positive trend: as average lagging increases, BLEU scores improve.
